Getting started¶

Requirements and installation¶

Use a checkout of this repository, Git, and a current version of uv. Python 3.14 is the tested baseline; .python-version pins 3.14.10. uv can download the pinned interpreter if it is absent. Initial setup requires network access and disk space for Python, NumPy, SciPy, Astropy, and Matplotlib.

From a terminal:

git clone https://github.com/benjym/poly-mpm.git
cd poly-mpm
uv sync --extra dev --locked
uv run --locked python -c "import numpy; from constit import SUPPORTED; print(SUPPORTED)"

uv sync installs the project as well as its dependencies. --extra dev includes pytest; omit it if you only want to run simulations. Run the commands below from the checkout root. The snippets use uv run so activation is not required. An existing checkout should use the branch containing these docs; older branches may still contain the scalar implementation.

Alternatively, with Python 3.14 already installed:

python3.14 -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate
python -m pip install -e '.[dev]'

On Windows PowerShell, activate with .venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1 instead. For this pip workflow, replace uv run --locked python below with python. The pip install resolves compatible dependency versions; uv.lock records the exact tested environment. Updating Python alone does not modernise an old checkout.

First complete simulation¶

Run the small elastic ball example:

uv run --locked python MPM.py ball

It simulates one second with 500 particles and 1,000 timesteps. The terminal shows progress and ends with a newline. Matplotlib runs without a GUI; figures are saved to disk, not opened in a window. Expect Continuum/*.png and MP/*.png under im/ball/elastic/. Wall-clock duration depends on your machine and plot rendering. Repeating a run in the same directory can overwrite its files.

The installed command is equivalent:

uv run --locked poly-mpm ball

A bounded preview¶

Some examples request millions of steps. The CLI takes an example name and its positional arguments; it has no --max-steps or --output options. Use the Python API for a short preview and a separate output directory:

uv run --locked python - <<'PY'
from initialise import get_parameters
from MPM import run

P, G, L = get_parameters(['ball'])
P.save_dir = 'im/ball-preview/'
P.savetime = P.dt
run(P, G, L, max_steps=3)
print(P.t, P.tstep, P.save_dir)
PY

This shell heredoc works in macOS/Linux shells. On Windows, put its Python body in preview.py and run uv run --locked python preview.py. Set output=False in run to suppress all output callbacks, including custom history recording. In that mode there will be no saved plots or arrays.

Choosing an example¶

  • ball: a small first run with elastic material and saved plots.

  • dp_unit_test / dp_rate_unit_test: Drucker-Prager loading histories; full runs have 50,000 / 5,000 steps respectively.

  • bi_seg_test 22 2 11: segregation at 22 degrees, two grain-size classes, and 11 vertical grid nodes. Replace 2 with 8 for eight classes. The input converts its angle argument to its internal signed-radian convention. This is a long research example; start with a bounded run.

The complete example matrix gives all required arguments and identifies unsupported inputs. Examples with arguments must receive them in the listed order; there is no general argument parser for their settings. Bounded smoke checks establish compatibility, not stability over every original run duration or physical calibration.

Supported material names are rigid, elastic, viscous, von_mises, pouliquen, bingham, dp, dp_rate, and linear_mu. See Constitutive model audit before selecting parameters. Retired and missing laws fail at initialisation; they are not silently replaced.

Checking the installation¶

With the dev extra installed:

uv run --locked --extra dev python -m pytest -q -W error::RuntimeWarning
uv run --locked python -m benchmarks.audit_examples --output /tmp/poly-mpm-examples.json

The tests and benchmark modules require the source checkout. The audit performs five bounded timesteps per supported example; its output file records each example’s status. On Windows, choose a writable output path instead of /tmp.

poly-mpm

2D material point method with grain-size segregation
